events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Super Typhoon Bavi is currently located about 670 miles to the
northwest of Chuuk near 14.5N 144.4E and is moving west-northwest at
13 mph. Maximum sustained winds are 175 mph.Chuuk sits on the far
southeastern edge of Bavi and its associated monsoonal regime.

20 kt south to southwest winds and seas of 10 feet will ease
further tonight and Tuesday. This is the final statement for Chuuk
State.

For more information on Super Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the
Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National Weather
Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone
Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Super Typhoon Bavi is currently located about 550 miles to the
northeast of Yap and 835 miles to the northeast of Koror, Palau near
14.5N 144.4E. Bavi is moving west-northwest at 13 mph. Maximum
sustained winds are 175 mph. Palau and Yap sit on the southern sector
of Bavi and its large circulation.

Although Yap and Palau are expected to remain outside of Bavi's direct
wind field, surging west to southwest winds around 20 to 30 knots with
gusts of 40-45 knots are expected to develop across Palau and Yap.
These stronger gusts are most likely to occur near heavier showers
and rainbands.

Hazardous marine conditions are on tap the next several days due to
the above conditions. Inter island travel will be hazardous and
dangerous surf will establish along west and north facing reefs
tonight. Conditions look to improve late this week into early next
week.

For more information on Super Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the
Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National Weather
Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone
Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW.

events.region: Northern Bristol; Western Plymouth; Eastern Plymouth; Southern Plymouth; Barnstable
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeastern Massachusetts, including the
following areas, Barnstable MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Northern
Bristol MA, Southern Plymouth MA and Western Plymouth MA.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rain are expected at times today into
Tuesday afternoon. Widespread rainfall amounts of 1-3 inches
are expected into Tuesday. However, narrow bands of
torrential rainfall may result in localized amounts of 4-6
inches of rain inside 6 hours.
It remains low confidence when and where these potential
narrow bands of heavy rainfall setup. However, if they occur
they will bring the potential for urban and/or small stream
flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: McHenry; Mercer; Oliver; Sheridan; Central and Southern Ward/Minot Area; Western McLean; Eastern McLean
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A period of strong south winds gusting up to 55 mph will continue
moving across parts of central North Dakota tonight. The winds
are being caused by nearby thunderstorms, but are occurring away
from the storms themselves, and may be accompanied by little to
no rain. The winds may increase quickly at your location and
remain strong for up to an hour before weakening. The strong
winds may cause difficult driving conditions, especially for high
profile vehicles. The winds may also result in downed tree
branches, and will blow around objects that are not secured.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Abundant lightning on dry fuels will likely create
new ignitions across the region. Any fires that develop could
spread rapidly. Numerous new fire starts could overwhelm
initial attack.

* AFFECTED AREA...For this evening, central and eastern Fire
Weather Zone 624 and southern and central Fire Weather Zone 625,
or eastern Klamath and southern and central Lake counties. For
Monday, northern Fire Weather Zones 624 and 625.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Moving north and northeast around 20 to 25
mph. Storm mode will be a mix of dry and wet thunderstorms.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Isolated gusts up to 45 mph.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
